knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

  fig.width = 6.5,
  fig.height = 3.6,
  fig.align = "center",
  dpi = 110

The `sqc` package accompanies a course in Statistical Quality Control. It has three parts:

1. **Constants** for control chart limits: `d2()`, `d3()`, `c4()`, and the table `qc_constants()`.
2. **Charts**: `qc_chart()` computes an $\bar{X}$ or $R$ chart, and `autoplot()` draws it with ggplot2.
3. **Example data**: `filler` and `filler_rotating`, the four-head bottle filler used in Week 1.

```{r}
library(sqc)
```

## Control chart constants

Let $W = R/\sigma$ be the range of $n$ independent standard normal values. For subgroups of size $n$ from a normal process,
$$E(R) = d_2\sigma, \qquad SD(R) = d_3\sigma, \qquad E(s) = c_4\sigma.$$
The constants are computed exactly, so any subgroup size $n \ge 2$ is allowed.

```{r}
d2(4)
d3(4)
c4(5)
```

`qc_constants()` returns the whole table used for control limits: $A_2 = 3/(d_2\sqrt{n})$ for the $\bar{X}$ chart, $D_3$ and $D_4$ for the $R$ chart, and $A_3$, $B_3$, $B_4$ for charts based on the sample standard deviation.

```{r}
knitr::kable(qc_constants(2:8), digits = 3)
```

Because $d_2$ is the mean of $W$, you can check it by simulation:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
mean(replicate(100000, diff(range(rnorm(4)))))   # simulated d2 for n = 4
d2(4)                                            # exact
```

## The example data

A four-head filler fills one bottle per head in each cycle. The target is 500 mL and the bottle-to-bottle standard deviation within a head is 1 mL, but head 3 runs 3 mL high. This is an assignable cause.

`filler` follows the **mixed-head plan**: in every sampled cycle, one bottle from each head forms a sample of size 4. `cycle` is the sample number.

```{r}
head(filler, 8)
```

`filler_rotating` follows the **rational subgroup plan**: 5 consecutive cycles from head 1, then 5 from head 2, head 3, head 4, then head 1 again. Each block of 5 bottles from one head is a subgroup.

```{r}
head(filler_rotating, 8)
```

## Computing and drawing a chart

`qc_chart()` takes subgroup data and a chart `type`, either `"xbar"` or `"R"`. With a data frame, name the measurement column (`value`) and the column that identifies the subgroup (`sample`), as in dplyr. Subgroups are plotted in the order they first appear.

```{r}
q <- qc_chart(filler, type = "xbar", value = fill_ml, sample = cycle)
q
```

The object stores what you need to build tables and your own figures:

```{r}
q$center       # center line
q$limits       # lower and upper control limits
q$sigma        # estimated within-subgroup standard deviation, R-bar / d2
head(q$statistics)   # the plotted subgroup means
```

To draw the chart, call `autoplot()`. The default title names the chart; add a title, subtitle, and axis label to say what the data are.

```{r}
autoplot(q,
         subtitle = "Mixed-head plan: one bottle from each head in every sample",
         ylab = "Sample mean (mL)")
```

The $R$ chart works the same way. Its lower limit is $\max(0, \bar R - 3d_3\hat\sigma)$, which is 0 for subgroups of size 6 or fewer.

```{r}
qc_chart(filler, type = "R", value = fill_ml, sample = cycle) |>
  autoplot(subtitle = "Mixed-head plan", ylab = "Sample range (mL)")
```

You can also supply a matrix with one row per subgroup and one column per observation. This is convenient for small examples worked by hand:

```{r}
x <- matrix(c(10.1, 9.8, 10.0, 10.3,
              10.2, 10.0, 9.9, 10.1,
              9.7, 10.4, 10.0, 9.9),
            nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
qc_chart(x, type = "xbar")
```

## Rational subgroups change the limits

The two plans measure the same process. The mixed-head plan puts the head differences **inside** every sample, which inflates the within-sample ranges and widens the limits. The rational subgroup plan keeps each subgroup within one head.

```{r}
mixed <- qc_chart(subset(filler, cycle <= 20), type = "xbar", value = fill_ml, sample = cycle)
rational <- qc_chart(filler_rotating, type = "xbar", value = fill_ml,
                     sample = (cycle - 1) %/% 5 + 1)

data.frame(
  plan = c("Mixed-head", "Rational subgroup"),
  subgroup_size = c(mixed$n, rational$n),
  sigma_hat = c(mixed$sigma, rational$sigma),
  LCL = c(mixed$limits[["lcl"]], rational$limits[["lcl"]]),
  UCL = c(mixed$limits[["ucl"]], rational$limits[["ucl"]]),
  signals = c(length(mixed$signals$beyond), length(rational$signals$beyond))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The true within-head standard deviation is 1 mL. The mixed-head estimate is nearly twice that, so the limits are too wide and the chart never signals. With rational subgroups, $\hat\sigma$ is close to 1 and the chart signals when head 3 is sampled:

```{r}
autoplot(rational,
         title = expression(bar(X) * " chart: rational subgroup plan"),
         subtitle = "Subgroups of 5 consecutive bottles from one head",
         ylab = "Subgroup mean (mL)")
```

## Phase I and Phase II

In Phase I the center line and limits are estimated from the data. In Phase II new subgroups are monitored against those limits, which are no longer re-estimated. Give `qc_chart()` the Phase I `center` and `sigma` to build a Phase II chart.

```{r}
set.seed(7)
phase1 <- matrix(rnorm(25 * 5, mean = 50, sd = 2), ncol = 5)   # in-control data
p1 <- qc_chart(phase1, type = "xbar")

shift <- rep(c(0, 3), c(10, 5))                                # mean shifts up by 3 at sample 11
phase2 <- matrix(rnorm(15 * 5, mean = 50 + shift, sd = 2), ncol = 5)
p2 <- qc_chart(phase2, type = "xbar", center = p1$center, sigma = p1$sigma)

autoplot(p2,
         subtitle = "Phase II: limits from Phase I; the mean shifts at sample 11",
         ylab = "Sample mean")
```

For an $R$ chart, supplying `sigma` sets the center line to $d_2\sigma$.

## Signals

`qc_chart()` flags two signals:

- a point **beyond the control limits**, and
- a **run** of 7 or more consecutive points on one side of the center line (the points from the 7th onward are flagged). Change the run length with `run_length`.

The indices of the flagged points are in `$signals`, and `as.data.frame()` gives one row per subgroup:

```{r}
p2$signals
as.data.frame(p2) |>
  subset(status != "No signal")
```

## Customizing the plot

`autoplot()` returns an ordinary ggplot object, so add layers and themes with `+`:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

autoplot(rational, subtitle = "Rational subgroup plan") +
  labs(caption = "Head 3 runs 3 mL high") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Function reference

| Task | Code |
|:--|:--|
| $\bar{X}$ chart from a matrix | `qc_chart(m, type = "xbar")` |
| $R$ chart from a data frame | `qc_chart(df, "R", value = x, sample = s)` |
| Draw a chart | `autoplot(q, title = "...", subtitle = "...")` |
| Fix the center line or $\sigma$ | `qc_chart(m, "xbar", center = 500, sigma = 1)` |
| Estimated $\sigma$, center, limits | `q$sigma`, `q$center`, `q$limits` |
| Plotted statistics and signals | `q$statistics`, `q$signals` |
| Constants | `d2(n)`, `d3(n)`, `c4(n)`, `qc_constants(n)` |
